answer: The Diversity in Pottery Decoration (Zkeverz) and Diversity in Pottery Form (ZKeform) time series first show opposite growth trends in the 18th century BCE (≈1700 BCE, Late Neolithic period). At BCE 1800 the raw z-values are Pottery Form = 0.74 and Pottery Decoration = −0.48; by BCE 1700 Pottery Form has declined by ΔForm = −1.87 (to −1.13) while Pottery Decoration has increased by ΔDecor = +1.45 (to +0.97). This is the earliest (and only) centennial transition across the BCE 4300 → BCE 500 horizon in which ΔPotteryForm < 0 and ΔPotteryDecoration > 0 — every earlier centennial step either moves both indicators in the same direction or shows no change. The result is identical when reproduced from time_series_data.csv (raw PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration columns, ignoring the *_inter linear-interpolation smear) and from capital.csv (matching ZKeform/Zkeverz transition at BCE 1700 in the LN period), confirming the signal is not an artefact of interpolation.

payload.hypothesis: Diversity in Pottery Form (ZKeform) and Diversity in Pottery Decoration (Zkeverz) first decouple in the 18th century BCE (≈1700 BCE, Late Neolithic period): at the BCE 1800 → BCE 1700 centennial transition Pottery Form falls from 0.74 to −1.13 (ΔForm = −1.87) while Pottery Decoration rises from −0.48 to +0.97 (ΔDecor = +1.45). This is the earliest (and unique) centennial step across the BCE 4300 → BCE 500 horizon where Pottery Decoration increases while Pottery Form declines, identified identically from the raw columns of time_series_data.csv and from capital.csv (BCE 1700, LN period).
payload.workflow:
1. Loaded time_series_data.csv (3,601 rows, CE −4100 → −500) and capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 500 → BCE 4300).
2. For capital.csv, converted European comma-decimal numerics to floats.
3. Selected the RAW centennial pottery samples (PotteryForm / PotteryDecoration in time_series_data.csv; ZKeform / Zkeverz in capital.csv). The *_inter linear-interpolation columns in time_series_data.csv were excluded to avoid smoothing away the centennial signal.
4. Sorted each frame oldest → newest (BCE descending), then computed per-century first-differences (ΔForm, ΔDecor) between adjacent rows.
5. Filtered to transitions with ΔForm < 0 AND ΔDecor > 0.
6. Verified uniqueness: time_series_data.csv → 1 match (BCE 1700); capital.csv → 1 match (BCE 1700, period LN). Both agree to two decimal places.
7. Reported the BCE 1700 diagnostic row (pre-values, post-values, Δvalues) and the per-century diff tables.
